When the posterior is close to Gaussian, GINN gives the estimates, their uncertainties and the evidence from a single optimization, and the same derivatives quantify departures from it.

papers.title: automodel: A Skill for Agentic Model Discovery
papers.authors: Marco Virgolin, Harry Desmond, Ester Bergantin, Giorgio Morales, John W. Sheppard, Luigi Romano, Alessandro Lucantonio
papers.abstract: The search for better models, whether expressed as analytical equations or neural architectures, has increasingly shifted from manual design toward data-driven automation. While a multitude of algorithms exist, ranging from exhaustive search to AlphaEvolve, recent advances in general-purpose coding agents such as Claude Code and OpenAI Codex raise the question: could providing such systems with a "model discovery recipe" be enough to discover or improve models? We present automodel, an agent skill for general model discovery. With case studies in astrophysics, cardiovascular dynamics, precision agriculture, traffic flow, and vehicle tire dynamics, we show how commercial agents equipped with automodel can successfully identify novel and scientifically-relevant models. Our findings suggest that encoding model-discovery methodology as a portable agent skill can provide a simple, interactive, powerful and broadly applicable alternative to domain-specific automated discovery pipelines. The skill is available at: https://github.com/unlayer-ai/automodel.

papers.title: Possible origins of the two γ-ray components C0 and C1 in IC 443
papers.authors: Yujun Xian, Huan Yu, Bo Wang, Jun Fang
papers.abstract: Recent LHAASO observations of IC~443 reveal that its high-energy $γ$-ray emission can be decomposed into two components with clearly distinct spatial morphologies and spectral properties, namely the compact component C0 and component C1 with an angular extent of 0.67$^\circ$. We aim to explain the $γ$-ray emission mechanisms responsible for the two components in IC~443 and to further investigate their respective possible astrophysical counterparts. We model components C0 and C1 independently using two different physical scenarios. For component C0, we adopt an SNR-MC hadronic model that accounts for finite source-size effects to describe the escape and diffusion of high-energy particles and their $γ$-ray production via pp interactions with the surrounding molecular clouds. For component C1 , we employ a spatially dependent multi-zone leptonic transport model and describe the evolution of high-energy electrons under the combined action of advection, diffusion, and energy losses using a Fokker--Planck-type equation. The model reproduces the SEDs of components C0 and C1 well. Component C0 exhibits a pronounced $π^0$-decay feature, and the maximum energy of its escaping particles reaches the PeV scale. The $γ$-ray emission from component C1 can be explained by inverse Compton scattering. Its diffusion coefficient is approximately two orders of magnitude lower than that in the surrounding interstellar medium, and no significant synchrotron counterpart is detected. The $γ$-ray emission from IC~443 involves the combined action of multiple physical mechanisms. Component C0 may be a potential PeVatron candidate, whereas component C1 may correspond to a potential TeV halo candidate.

papers.title: Reconstructing the mass-redshift distribution of supermassive black holes using multiband gravitational-wave observations
papers.authors: Alorika Kar, Souvik Jana, Enrico Barausse, Parameswaran Ajith
papers.abstract: The formation and evolution of supermassive black holes (SMBHs) remain major open questions in astrophysics. Astrophysical models of SMBHs invoke black-hole (BH) seeds formed at high redshift, which subsequently grow through gas accretion and mergers. Although observations of high-redshift quasars and active galactic nuclei constrain these scenarios, the mechanisms governing SMBH formation and growth remain uncertain. Future gravitational-wave (GW) observations across the millihertz, decihertz, and audio-frequency bands will provide a complementary and direct probe of SMBH assembly by tracing their merger history. We investigate the extent to which multiband GW observations can reconstruct the mass-redshift distribution of these mergers. We simulate populations of BH mergers predicted by different astrophysical models and identify those observable by the millihertz detector LISA, the decihertz detector LGWA, and next-generation ground-based detectors operating in the audio-frequency band. We reconstruct the mass-redshift distribution of these mergers using the nonparametric inference code FIGARO. We find that combining observations across frequency bands substantially improves the reconstruction for the light-seed models considered here, whose merger populations span broad ranges of mass and redshift. In contrast, for the heavy-seed models considered here, LISA alone recovers most of the accessible mass-redshift distribution, with little additional improvement from the multiband network.

papers.title: Design and performance of the front-end readout electronics for LACT
papers.authors: Changge Zi, Jinfan Chang, Fengfan Yang, Ming Wei, Wei Wei
papers.abstract: The Large Array of Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescope (LACT) will complement the Large High Altitude Air Shower Observatory (LHAASO) with a target angular resolution of 0.05 degrees to resolve the morphology of Very-High-Energy gamma-ray sources. The array is designed to comprise 32 telescopes with 6-meter apertures within LHAASO at an altitude of approximately 4410 meters. Each camera contains 1616 silicon photomultipliers (SiPMs). We developed a front-end readout electronics (FEE) board integrating 16 channels of SiPM gain compensation and high-speed waveform sampling for operation at high altitude and over a wide temperature range. The gain compensation circuit independently adjusts the operating voltage of each SiPM according to its temperature and monitors the actual operating voltage. Previous tests of the adopted compensation scheme showed SiPM gain drift below 2% from -20 to 30 degrees Celsius. The waveform sampling circuit uses two 14-bit AC9628 analog-to-digital converters, each operating in eight-channel mode, to digitize the SiPM pulse waveform at 250 million samples per second. The integral nonlinearity of the DC response is 0.0709% over a differential DC voltage range of -950 mV to +950 mV at the AC9628 input. Equivalent electrical pulses with a full width at half maximum of 37.42 ns are used to simulate the SiPM output signals. At a differential pulse amplitude of approximately 237 mV at the AC9628 input, the pulse integral area resolution is 0.2725%. This paper presents the circuit design and performance tests of the FEE for the LACT camera.

papers.abstract: Cosmic-ray particles in the TeV range, originating outside the solar system, are partially blocked on their way to Earth by the Moon, producing a deficit in their flux known as the Moon shadow. This work presents a precision measurement of the westward shift of the Moon's shadow using 3.4 years of data from LHAASO's Water Cherenkov Detector Array (WCDA). We use this direct physical measurement, combined with four cosmic-ray composition models, each divided into five mass groups, to calibrate the detector's absolute energy response in the range of 4 - 37 TeV. We quantify the fractional deviation between the calibrated and simulated energy scales by determining a best-fit scale shift parameter of $ε$ =-0.04 $\pm$ 0.03. This yields a 95% confidence interval of -9% to +0.2% for the systematic energy scale deviation. Complementing the simulation based on hadronic interaction model, this geomagnetic calibration provides a data-driven physical validation of the simulated WCDA energy response, effectively bounding systematic uncertainties and refining the overall energy scale.

papers.title: A Tight Broad-line Width-Luminosity Relation in Little Red Dots and Its Consequence for Virial Black Hole Masses
papers.authors: Haoyu Wang
papers.abstract: JWST has uncovered compact high-redshift sources with red, $\sim 5000$ K optical continua and broad Balmer lines, known as "little red dots" (LRDs). Whether these lines trace gas orbiting a massive black hole or electron scattering in a dense, Eddington-limited envelope around a lighter black hole leaves inferred masses spanning $10^{4}$--$10^{8}\,M_\odot$. We test both pictures by uniformly refitting public JWST/NIRSpec spectra of 29 LRDs, 15 other JWST broad-line sources, and luminosity-matched SDSS quasars. At fixed $\mathrm{H}α$ luminosity, LRD broad $\mathrm{H}α$ widths are remarkably uniform: their intrinsic scatter is 0.054 dex ($<0.075$ dex at 95%), less than half that of quasars (0.12 dex), clustering near $1760\ \mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ outside the three brightest sources. Because single-epoch virial masses scale as width squared, they scatter intrinsically by $<0.16$ dex at fixed $\mathrm{H}α$ luminosity, making virial masses and mass functions nearly deterministic restatements of luminosity regardless of the underlying physics. Compared with the Keplerian speed $v_{\rm K}$ at the photosphere of an Eddington-limited envelope, computed from each source's measured continuum luminosity and temperature, observed widths are $2.5$--$3.0\,v_{\rm K}$ ($2\text{--}3\times$ standard expectations for virial factors $f_{\rm vir}\approx0.5\text{--}1$), with a quarter of the flux above escape speed and no detected continuum-luminosity dependence at fixed $\mathrm{H}α$ luminosity. Bound orbits outside a spherical photosphere thus require sub-Eddington luminosities ($\leq 0.10\text{--}0.30\,L_{\rm Edd}$), whereas an Eddington or super-Eddington envelope requires uniform $2\text{--}3\times$ non-gravitational broadening within the $\mathrm{H}α$-emitting gas.

papers.title: SN 2025wiu: A Slowly Evolving Type Ib Supernova with an Extraordinary Post-maximum Bump
papers.authors: Zhengyan Liu, Ji-an Jiang, Zelin Xu, Qiliang Fang, Keiichi Maeda, Hanindyo Kuncarayakti, Lluís Galbany, Saurabh W. Jha, Željko Ivezić, Peter Yoachim, Andrew J. Connolly, Dezheng Meng, Weiyu Wu, Ziqing Jia, Niko Pyykkinen, Masaomi Tanaka, Nozomu Tominaga, Junhan Zhao, Ming Chen, Tiancheng Lv, Tinggui Wang, Zigao Dai, Xu Kong, Luhan Li, Bo Wang, Jianguo Wang, Yongquan Xue, Wen Zhao, Qingfeng Zhu, Lulu Fan, Feng Li, Ming Liang, Binyang Liu, Zhen Wan, Hairen Wang, Jian Wang, Ji Yang, Hongfei Zhang, Xianzhong Zheng
papers.abstract: Stripped-envelope supernovae (SESNe) originate from massive progenitors that have lost most or all of their outer envelopes prior to core collapse. Recent advances in optical time-domain surveys have revealed a growing population of peculiar SESNe with unusual light-curve morphologies, pointing to energy sources beyond the standard radioactive-decay scenario. In this work, we present multi-band photometric and spectroscopic observations of SN 2025wiu, a peculiar Type Ib supernova discovered by the Wide Field Survey Telescope (WFST). SN 2025wiu is characterized by a high luminosity and exceptionally slow photometric evolution, with a prominent post-maximum bump peaking at $\sim50$ days after the primary maximum. Its early light curve also shows a weak excess consistent with shock-cooling emission from a compact progenitor with a radius of $\sim4\,R_\odot$. The spectra show only modest evolution, with persistently weak line features and no narrow emission lines detected even at $\sim110$ days after maximum. By modeling the primary peak and late-time tail with a combination of radioactive decay and additional energy sources, we isolate the post-maximum bump, which has a roughly symmetric profile with a peak luminosity of $\sim2.4 \times 10^{42}~\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ and a characteristic duration of $\sim42$ days. We discuss circumstellar medium (CSM) interaction, accretion, magnetar activity, and a double $^{56}$Ni distribution as possible origins of the bump. The latter three scenarios face challenges in reproducing the post-maximum bump, while delayed CSM interaction remains a possible explanation.

papers.title: WFST0533buha (Bi'an): A Fast Blue Ultraluminous Transient Candidate with Unusual Blue/NUV Colors
papers.authors: Zelin Xu, Ji-an Jiang, Ziqing Jia, Keiichi Maeda, Dezheng Meng, Zhengyan Liu, Weiyu Wu, Junhan Zhao, Hanindyo Kuncarayakti, Lluís Galbany, Saurabh W. Jha, Željko Ivezić, Peter Yoachim, Andrew J. Connolly, Tao An, Ming Chen, Zigao Dai, Xu Kong, Tiancheng Lv, Masaomi Tanaka, Nozomu Tominaga, Ailing Wang, Ning Jiang, Yongquan Xue, Wen Zhao, Qingfeng Zhu, Lulu Fan, Feng Li, Ming Liang, Binyang Liu, Zhen Wan, Hairen Wang, Jian Wang, Ji Yang, Hongfei Zhang, Xianzhong Zheng
papers.abstract: We present WFST0533buha (Bi'an), a fast blue ultraluminous transient (FBUT) candidate discovered by the Wide Field Survey Telescope Deep High-cadence $ugr$-band Survey. The source brightened by approximately 2.5 mag in $u$ within 3 days and has a half-maximum timescale ($t_{1/2}$) shorter than 6 days. Two spectra show a blue, featureless continuum but do not provide a secure redshift. Einstein Probe observations yield only X-ray upper limits, while a faint radio counterpart was detected at 15 GHz with the VLA. The early $u$-band detection and intensive multiband coverage of Bi'an demonstrate the value of deep, high-cadence blue-band observations for discovering and characterizing FBUTs at early phases. Notably, Bi'an shows redder blue/NUV colors than AT 2018cow and AT 2024wpp, suggesting possible diversity in the short-wavelength properties of FBUTs.

papers.title: A Butterfly Collector's View of Fast Radio Bursts: Repeating Sources Go Quiet within a Few Years
papers.authors: Shotaro Yamasaki
papers.abstract: How long repeating fast radio burst (FRB) sources stay active is key to their origins but poorly known as a population. We test this with unseen species estimation, a method first used to predict how many new butterfly species a further collecting trip would find. If each source keeps the same mean rate over time, the number of sources seen $k+1$ times in one window predicts how many bursts the sources seen $k$ times will emit in a later window. It assumes neither the burst rate distribution nor source distances. For the five years of CHIME/FRB Catalog 2, we measure the ratio $R$ of observed to predicted bursts against the gap $Δ$ between windows. A steady mean rate gives $R = 1$ at every $Δ$, so a change of $R$ with $Δ$ means that the sources change. $R$ is close to unity for $Δ\lesssim 60$ days and drops by half within one year. Neither steady nor randomly fluctuating sources reproduce this decline, unless the latter are mostly silent. Three models explain the data equally well: a lifetime of about three years, on/off activity with two-year active phases, or a mix of short- and long-lived sources. Fitted to the first three years alone, they correctly predict the further decline of $R$ in the last two years. Longer monitoring of $R$, and of whether silent sources come back to life, will distinguish them. Unlike butterfly species, FRB sources do not wait for the next collecting trip, so follow-up should start soon.

papers.title: Probing the Turbulent Magnetised Interstellar Medium of the Small Magellanic Cloud through Depolarisation with POSSUM Observations
papers.authors: Jason M. Price, Yik Ki Ma, Amit Seta, N. M. McClure-Griffiths, B. M. Gaensler, S. Lyla Jung, Cameron L. Van Eck, David McConnell, Lindsey Oberhelman, J. D. Livingston, Takuya Akahori, Shane P. O'Sullivan, Denis Leahy, C. S. Anderson
papers.abstract: The interstellar medium (ISM) of the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC) provides a unique laboratory for studying magnetised gas in a low-metallicity, tidally disturbed environment. We investigate this magnetised turbulent medium using broad-band polarimetric data from the Australian Square Kilometre Array Pathfinder (ASKAP)'s Polarisation Sky Survey of the Universe's Magnetism (POSSUM), leveraging a high-density Rotation Measure (RM) grid comprising 951 RMs ($\sim24$ RMs per square degree) to probe the magneto-ionic structure of the SMC. We statistically compare the number densities of polarised and non-polarised non-thermal background sources on a per-square-degree basis, revealing spatially coherent depolarisation signatures that correlate with enhanced plane-of-sky RM fluctuations. This is consistent with a turbulent cascade from large-scale structures. Analysed through RM synthesis and Stokes $QU$-fitting, we attribute the depolarisation to a turbulent magneto-ionic medium within the telescope's beam ($\lesssim6~\mathrm{pc}$). Faraday complexity is detected in $\sim$24% of the RM sources; however, no coherent spatial structure is observed in the complexity distribution, and we attribute this primarily to internal source structure or an extended halo surrounding the SMC rather than to its main body. Furthermore, as previously identified in the Large Magellanic Cloud, depolarisation in the SMC increases with emission measure; however, the underlying Faraday dispersion is $\sim$6 times weaker. With the thermal electron density smooth on the scales of the field fluctuations, this depolarisation is likely driven by magnetic field fluctuations.

papers.title: SPONGE: Sulphur, Phosphorus, Oxygen, Nitrogen, and carbon Galactic Evolution. I. CNOPS elements as probes of physical processes in stars and galaxies
papers.authors: D. Romano, M. Limongi, E. Caffau, Y. P. Zou, P. Bonifacio, L. Monaco, L. Colzi, E. Spitoni, M. Palla, S. Tsiatsiou, D. Nandal, J. Alazzawi, A. Falla, F. Fontani, A. J. Gallagher, R. Hirschi, F. Lucertini, A. Mucciarelli, L. Roberti, M. Spite, M. Steffen
papers.abstract: As fundamental bio-essential elements, carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, phosphorus, and sulphur (CNOPS) warrant a precise mapping of their cosmic origins. In this paper, we present the SPONGE project (Sulphur, Phosphorus, Oxygen, Nitrogen, and carbon Galactic Evolution), aimed at establishing a self-consistent galactic chemical evolution (GCE) framework capable of simultaneously reproducing local abundance benchmarks along with key observational constraints in external galaxies. Here, we focus on the Milky Way. We compile literature data and construct GCE models incorporating various single- and binary-star yields, taking stellar rotation and nova nucleosynthesis into account. Fast rotators are confirmed to be essential for primary 14N and 13C production at low metallicities. Although our homogeneous models do not reach the lowest 12C/13C ratios observed in some halo stars, this discrepancy should not be taken as a refutation of the model, as observational selection effects may apply. Predicted C and N isotopic ratios along the disc agree remarkably well with those inferred from radio observations of star-forming regions. Notably, our models explain Galactic P enrichment as originating predominantly from massive stars, without any ad hoc adjustment of the yields or the need for a significant nova contribution. Conversely, novae are required to synthesize non-negligible fractions of 13C and 15N. Optimizing GCE trajectories against a comprehensive CNOPS ensemble simultaneously, rather than single diagnostics one at a time, establishes a robust baseline for future work. Remaining open questions, such as the predicted overproduction of 12C at low metallicities and 34S along the disc, alongside the abundance scatter of some key elements, provide concrete targets for subsequent papers in this series.

papers.authors: Rainer Schödel, Adam Ginsburg, Steve Longmore, John Bally, Francisco Nogueras-Lara, Samantha Adams, María Álvarez-Santiago, Pau Amaro Seoane, Konstantina Anastasopoulou, Mayura Balakrishnan, Ashley T. papers.abstract: The center of the Milky Way is the densest and most extreme environment in our Galaxy, its most active star forming region, and the only galaxy nucleus where we can resolve stars down to about a solar mass on the main sequence. The Galactic Center (GC) contains a nuclear stellar disk, a nuclear star cluster, and a supermassive black hole, all embedded within the so-called Central Molecular Zone, which showcases conditions of the interstellar medium that are typically found in high-redshift star-forming regions. The GC hosts the highest concentration of massive stars in the Milky Way and hosts a large concentration of rare objects, such as Wolf Rayet stars and X-ray binaries. The GC is therefore an astrophysical target of outstanding importance. A multi-epoch JWST program enables novel science including the lifetime of planet-forming disks, the search for intermediate mass black holes, direct measurements of the multi-scale gravitational potential, and a deep measurement of the star formation history. Multi-epoch imaging observations with JWST's NIRCam and MIRI instruments will go far beyond Roman WFI surveys in terms of depth and astrometric and photometric precision because of its $3\times$ better resolution, and it expands spectral coverage in narrow bands and mid-infrared wavelength coverage. The proposed observations would correspond to a Treasury Program of about 420\,h, distributed over three epochs spaced three to five years apart.

papers.title: Enabling joint chemical and meteorological data assimilation with an atmospheric foundation model
papers.authors: Eliot J. Kim, Eric J. Mei, Peter D. Ivatt, Lee T. Murray, Alexander J. Turner
papers.abstract: The hydroxyl radical (OH) is the main oxidant in the troposphere and accounts for 88% of the methane sink, yet its abundance and trends remain poorly constrained. Satellites observe many of the chemical and meteorological drivers of OH, but assimilating both requires a model that represents chemistry and meteorology together. Existing chemistry-climate models are too expensive for joint data assimilation. Here, we present AuroraChem, a fine-tuned version of the Aurora atmospheric foundation model that jointly simulates meteorology and the GEOS-Chem chemical fields needed to constrain OH. A one-year AuroraChem rollout takes 12 minutes on one GPU. Free rollouts remain stable for one year but do not fully capture seasonal cycles. Using idealized data assimilation, we find that chemical observations can constrain the meteorological state and meteorological observations can constrain the chemical state. Inserting only the chemical fields raises the annual mean spatial correlation of 500 hPa temperature from 0.89 to 0.92 and recovers the moisture and circulation pattern of the Indian summer monsoon. Inserting only the meteorological fields raises the 500 hPa OH correlation from 0.89 to 0.93, close to the 0.94 from inserting the chemical fields themselves, and recovers the OH seasonal cycle. Inserting only NO2 columns sampled at TROPOMI pixels gives an OH correlation of 0.93. These relationships likely reflect learned covariances rather than physical coupling, and covariances are what data assimilation uses to let an observation of one variable update the others. AuroraChem therefore provides a new pathway to joint chemical and meteorological data assimilation.

papers.title: Multifrequency deep radio continuum VLA observations toward OMC-2/3
papers.authors: Ana K. Diaz-Rodriguez, Mayra Osorio, Guillem Anglada, S. Thomas Megeath, John J. Tobin, Elise Furlan, M. Dolores Hurtado-Espejo, A. Florin Placinta-Mitrea, José F. Gómez, Guillermo Blázquez-Calero, William J. Fischer, P. Manoj, Dan M. Watson, Amelia M. Stutz, Luis F. Rodríguez
papers.abstract: We present multiwavelength (0.7-5 cm) Very Large Array continuum observations of high sensitivity (3 $μ$Jy beam$^{-1}$), reaching an angular resolution of $0.4''$ (154 au) toward the Integral Shaped Filament in Orion. We image a field of $12.5'$ in diameter, containing the whole OMC-2 region and the southernmost $2.5'$ of OMC-3. We report the positions, flux densities and spectral indices of 47 radio sources, and discuss their nature. We conclude that, out of the 57 radio sources in the field of view, 36 (63%) are very likely tracing YSOs, 4 are tracing jet/outflow knots, and 6 are extragalactic sources; the nature of the remaining sources is unclear. We identify the driving sources of the 9 previously reported molecular outflows in our field of view. Four of them show a clear elongated radio jet morphology. We detect free-free emission from two potential photoevaporating discs associated with Class III YSOs. We find variability in 11 radio sources, 7 of which are also variable at shorter wavelengths. We find 7 pairs of radio sources with projected separations of 150-3000 au, which are potential binary systems; we identify a total of 17 potential multiple systems within this separation range when taking into account sources detected at other wavelengths. This work highlights the potential of deep VLA observations to uncover a large population of weak radio sources and study their diversity, serving as a guide for future surveys with the SKA and ngVLA.

papers.title: Two Faint Tidal Disruption Events Discovered in a Pilot Search with the Wide Field Survey Telescope
papers.authors: Mingxin Wu, Ning Jiang, Jiazheng Zhu, Jianwei Lyu, Zheyu Lin, Yibo Wang, Tinggui Wang, Chengyi Wang, Weiyu Wu, Jie Lin, Zelin Xu, Minxuan Cai, Ranfang Zheng, Lulu fan, Ji-an Jiang, Xu Kong, Feng Li, Ming Liang, Binyang Liu, Zhen Wan, Hairen Wang, Jian Wang, Yongquan Xue, Hongfei Zhang, Wen Zhao, Xianzhong Zheng, Qingfeng Zhu
papers.abstract: We report the discovery of TDE 2025alrm/WFST250129blnve and TDE 2025amkg/WFST251021dbmwk in the first six months of the wide-field survey (WFS) performed by the 2.5-meter Wide Field Survey Telescope (WFST). Both events are apparently faint among known optical tidal disruption events (TDEs), with peak magnitudes of $g \sim 20.0$ and $g \sim 19.6$, respectively. Blackbody fits to the multi-band photometry yield roughly constant temperatures of $\sim 10^{4}$ K for both sources, with peak bolometric luminosities of $10^{43.6}$ erg s$^{-1}$ and $10^{43.8}$ erg s$^{-1}$, respectively. Optical spectra obtained during the declining phase display characteristic broad Balmer, He II, and N III emission lines, classifying both sources as H+He TDEs. Host-galaxy SED fitting suggests stellar masses on the order of $10^{9} M_{\odot}$ and black hole masses of $\sim10^{6} M_{\odot}$, which are typical of optically selected TDE hosts. The pilot discovery of these two faint TDEs along with dozens of candidates, demonstrates the capability of WFST to discover TDEs, owing to its exceptional survey depth. Furthermore, these events highlight the value of the $u$ band in multi-band surveys for TDE selection, particularly for distinguishing TDEs from supernovae at early phases. With continued operations, WFST is expected to substantially expand the known TDE population, especially by uncovering nearby low-luminosity events and high-redshift TDEs, both of which remain poorly explored.

papers.title: Positron escape from dark matter spikes in black hole X-ray binaries
papers.authors: Mpho Kgoadi, Geoff Beck
papers.abstract: Chan and Lee present a model where the AMS-02 positron excess is explained by dark matter (DM) annihilation in spike halos around nearby black holes A0620-00 and XTE J1118+480. Their model assumes a uniform magnetic and diffusive environment en route to Earth. Thus, it depends on the assumption that one can ignore the small-scale, near-horizon environment in the diffusion-loss equation. We demonstrate that this is not the case. An accurate magnetic field model near the horizon means, without increasing the required cross-section by a factor of roughly 500 to 1400, depending on the transport near the horizon, the positron flux from these sources cannot account for a significant fraction of the AMS-02 excess.
